window.description: For a Java program: a part of its main window's title, to find it ('SRK', 'Oracle Applications').
window.title: Window

timezone.description: Time zone the process is done in (IANA, e.g. Europe/Warsaw); runs use it, so a date typed on screen means the same as when people type it.
timezone.title: Timezone

locale.description: Browser language the process is done in, e.g. pl-PL.
locale.title: Locale

Calendar.description: How a calendar shows its days and months and how it moves, for 'pick_date'.

day.description: How a day is named: '{d} {month} {yyyy}' for '24 listopada 2026', '{d}' for days that are only numbers (fields of maptelo.dates).
day.title: Day

days.description: What a day of the calendar is: a role (gridcell, button) or a CSS selector, without a name.

month.description: How the month shown over the days is named ('{Month_en} {yyyy}' for 'October 2026'), when the days do not say their month and year.
month.title: Month

box.description: The calendar: where its days, its month and its arrows are.
box.title: Box

next.description: What moves it to the next month.
next.title: Next

previous.description: What moves it a month back.
previous.title: Previous

opens.description: The step's target opens the calendar (it is clicked first); false for a calendar always shown, the step's target being the calendar itself.
opens.title: Opens

Calendar.title: Calendar

DayShift.description:
A date the record does not give, counted from another of its dates (the old price
line ends the day before the new one starts: ``{from: start_date, days: -1}``).

from.description: The date input it is counted from.
from.title: From

days.description: Days after that date; negative: before it.
days.title: Days

working.description: The days are working days: Saturdays, Sundays and the public holidays of 'holidays' are skipped (-1: the last working day before the date, as the NBP rate of a tax point).
working.title: Working

holidays.description: The country whose public holidays are no working days (PL).
holidays.title: Holidays

DayShift.title: DayShift

DialogAnswer.description:
How a dialog of the browser itself, brought up by the step, is answered: as the
person answered it in the recording („Zapisać zmiany?” OK, „Podaj powód” with a value).

value.description: For a prompt: what to type ('$inputs.x' for the data's).
value.title: Value

DialogAnswer.title: DialogAnswer

DocumentField.description:
For 'read' of a document image (a scan, a photo): the field read with a model that sees
images, checked by the rules of its kind before it is used (the full Maptelo reads them).

field.description: The field as the document and the form name it.
field.title: Field

role.description: Which amount it is, for the document's net + VAT = gross check.
role.title: Role

typed_as.description: How the form writes it: a date's pattern (%d.%m.%Y) or the value's shape with 9 for every digit (9 999,99); without it the value is typed as printed.
typed_as.title: Typed As

compare_with.description: The field on the screen holding another reading of the same value (what OCR put in the form). A value no rule checks (a number, a date) is taken only when the two readings agree; a tax number or an account the picture does not give is taken from it when it passes its check.
compare_with.title: Compare With

DocumentField.title: DocumentField

Effect.description: A change in the system of record that defines 'done'.
Effect.title: Effect

Evidence.description: Where a step or rule came from: recordings that support it and who confirmed it.
Evidence.title: Evidence

retryable.description: Default: system exceptions yes, business exceptions no.
retryable.title: Retryable

FieldCheck.description: Value of a form field, found by label or by a target ladder.

gt.description: The number it shows is greater.
gt.title: Gt

gte.description: The number it shows is at least this.
gte.title: Gte

lt.description: The number it shows is smaller.
lt.title: Lt

lte.description: The number it shows is at most this.
lte.title: Lte

FieldCheck.title: FieldCheck

FindMade.description:
The owner's way to find the document a save made, when its answer was lost (benchmark
"faults", p10: „Utwórz przesyłkę” answered by a gateway error, the parcel made at the
courier): ``read`` holds when the record's document is there, and finds none (404) when it
is not; the document is opened from ``list``, in the row ``row``, by ``open``. Then the steps
after the save go on with that document, and no second one is made.

list.description: The list's address, as a 'navigate' step's value.
list.title: List

row.description: The record's row on the list: its table and values.

open.description: What opens the document in that row.
open.title: Open

FindMade.title: FindMade

HttpVerifier.description: Reads the system of record through a channel other than the screen that wrote it.

url.description: Absolute URL or path relative to application.api_base_url; {inputs.name} placeholders allowed.
url.title: Url

expect.description: Response JSON field -> expected value ($inputs.name allowed).
expect.title: Expect

when_missing.description: Response field -> exact empty value (empty string or null) when its expected input is absent. The field must still be present in the response. Only direct $inputs.name expectations may declare this contract.
when_missing.title: When Missing

HttpVerifier.title: HttpVerifier

Idempotency.description: If these effects already hold before a run, the work is done: skip instead of redo.
Idempotency.title: Idempotency

column.description: Header of the column in the records file (a sheet or CSV) that holds this value, when people take it from a table.
column.title: Column

typed_as.description: How people type the value on screen: a date pattern such as %d.%m.%Y or %m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S, 0.00 / 0,00 for an amount with two decimals, zeros (000000000) for a number typed to that width with its leading zeros, or national for a phone number typed without its country's code (+1 2058812302 as 2058812302).
typed_as.title: Typed As

written_as.description: How the records file writes a date as text, when not as YYYY-MM-DD: a pattern such as %m/%d/%Y (09/10/2012), %d.%m.%Y or %d/%B/%Y (15/November/2026), Oracle's DD-MON-YYYY (15-NOV-2026), or excel: Excel's number of the day, as a CSV file saved from a sheet may write it (46326 for 2026-10-31).
written_as.title: Written As

taken_after.description: The value is the part of the column's text after these signs, the last time they stand in it (the order's number 5510 of the price list's name „CENNIK_ZK_5510”: _ZK_); a value without them is taken whole.
taken_after.title: Taken After

secret.description: A password or a key: never shown nor kept (results, logs, messages show it masked).
secret.title: Secret

per_line.description: One value for each line of the record (the products of an order): the steps that use it are done once per line.
per_line.title: Per Line

per_column.description: The column whose number divides this one's value (a price for 1000 pieces: „Cena za” says 1000 szt.); the value typed is the one for a single unit.
per_column.title: Per Column

derived.description: A date counted from another date of the record (the day before it: days -1); the records file needs no column for it.

Interrupt.description: A state that may appear at any moment (popup, session warning) and its handler.
Interrupt.title: Interrupt

Locator.description: One rung of a target ladder. Exactly one strategy is set.

column.description: Header of the table column the element is in (for a definition: its term, as in 'Numer rachunku: PL61...'); only with 'role'.
column.title: Column

field.description: The name a form sends the value under (name attribute), on the control or on the one element around a lone control; it rarely changes when the words do.
field.title: Field

submits.description: The button that sends the form holding the field of this name (its only submit button); an update renames the button more often than what it sends.
submits.title: Submits

beside.description: A field nothing names (no label of its own), by the words beside it in its own row or box („Genre:”), as a person reads which field it is.
beside.title: Beside

action.description: A button by the name of what it does in the application (<button name="action_confirm">, as Odoo writes them): it stays when the words change or are translated.
action.title: Action

Locator.title: Locator

PageVerifier.description:
Reads the record again on a page of the web application itself, opened afresh by its
address after the work, as a person reloads a list to see the new row: a fresh page shows
what the system stored, not what the screen said after saving. The same application, so
weaker than an API of its own; proposed from the recordings and confirmed by a person,
never assumed (the clean-Windows test of 11.10: a person who knows no API).

url.description: The page: a path on the application (its base_url) or an absolute address; {inputs.name} placeholders allowed.
url.title: Url

table.description: The table's name, when one is shown.
table.title: Table

row.description: Column -> the value that names the record's row ($inputs.name allowed).
row.title: Row

expect.description: Column -> the value the record's row shows ($inputs.name allowed).
expect.title: Expect

PageVerifier.title: PageVerifier

Predicate.description: An observable condition. Exactly one kind is set; all/any/not combine others.

url.description: Glob matched against the page path; a #part (key=glob&...) must match too.
url.title: Url

Predicate.title: Predicate

ProcessCard.description:
What the process is for, in the words of the people who do it: what no recording shows
(Maptelo Lite asks for it after recording; the SOP and the AI brief start with it).

story.description: The process in the person's own words, as told to someone new on the team: where the data comes from, what is done in which program, what goes otherwise.
story.title: Story

goal.description: What the process achieves, and for whom.
goal.title: Goal

data.description: Where its values come from (a sheet, a mail, a portal).
data.title: Data

scope.description: What a robot may do, and what stays with a person.
scope.title: Scope

done.description: How one knows the work is done, and where one checks it.
done.title: Done

failures.description: What goes wrong at times, and what is done then.
failures.title: Failures

ProcessCard.title: ProcessCard

ReadRequest.description: An owner-confirmed form POST that only reads, scoped to one step and application.
ReadRequest.title: ReadRequest

RecordsSpec.description:
Where the rows of a batch come from when people work from a table (a sheet of a
workbook or a CSV file): one run per row. Inputs name their ``column``; other columns
of the table are left alone.

sheet.description: Sheet of the workbook (default: the first one).
sheet.title: Sheet

one_run_per.description: Columns that name one record when several rows make it (an order and its products): rows with the same values are one run, each row one of its lines.
one_run_per.title: One Run Per

RecordsSpec.title: RecordsSpec

RepeatUntil.description:
A click done again until something shows: a status a system gives later („Sprawdź
status w KSeF” until the invoice has its number). People click it a few times, waiting in
between; the robot does the same, and leaves the record to a person if it does not come.

tries.description: How many times at most the click is done.
tries.title: Tries

every_ms.description: How long to wait for it before clicking again.
every_ms.title: Every Ms

RepeatUntil.title: RepeatUntil

ScreenVerifier.description:
Reads the record again in the program itself, on a screen other than the one that
wrote it, as a person checks a list after saving: a desktop program has no API. The
screen is opened from the menu, the record's row is found in its table by the values that
name it, and the row's cells are compared.

menu.description: The menu, then its item: ['Ceny', 'Wnioski cenowe'].
menu.title: Menu

row.description: Column -> the value that names the record's row ($inputs.name allowed).
row.title: Row

expect.description: Column -> the value the record's row shows ($inputs.name allowed).
expect.title: Expect

rows.description: 'one': the values name the record's one row; 'all': the record wrote several rows the values name (the lines of an imported file, benchmark M3), each to show what expect says.
rows.title: Rows

ScreenVerifier.title: ScreenVerifier

State.description: A screen the process can be on, recognised by its fingerprint.

url.description: Glob matched against the page path; a #part (key=glob&...) must match too.
url.title: Url

visible.description: All of these must be visible.
visible.title: Visible

State.title: State

intent.description: What the step achieves, in business terms.
intent.title: Intent

note.description: What the person who showed the process said about the step, while showing it or on its map afterwards: why it is done, the rule they follow („the newest SBI”).
note.title: Note

note_when.description: When the step is done, as the person said it („only when the invoice's amount differs from the WZ”): for people and for whoever builds the automation; a robot follows only a rule (when).
note_when.title: Note When

person_decides.description: The person said a person decides at this step: a robot stops before it.
person_decides.title: Person Decides

alternatives.description: The other decisions offered where this one was chosen („Korekta (CN)” beside „Akceptuj” in the invoice's row): no recording showed when they are made. Unless the owner says it is always this one, a person decides, or the robot makes it only while its rule ('requires') holds and stops before it otherwise.
alternatives.title: Alternatives

document.description: For 'read' with a target that is a document's image: which field of the document to read.

save_as.description: Variable set by 'read' (the text) or 'download' (where the file is kept).
save_as.title: Save As

after.description: For 'read' without a target: the words the value follows in what the screen says, in the page or a frame of it („Zgłoszono szkodę” SZK/2026/0001., „Termin dostawy:” 2026-10-20); the value is the word after them.
after.title: After

looks_like.description: With 'after': what the value looks like, letters A and digits 9 (A-9 for PO-10001, 9-9-9 for a date); a word after the same words shaped otherwise is not it.
looks_like.title: Looks Like

rest.description: With 'after': the value is the whole rest of the message the words label („Kontrole: Kwota poza tolerancją…”), not the one word after them.
rest.title: Rest

match.description: For 'select_option': the option is the one whose name's words all stand in the value (the customer an e-mail names), and no other with as many; without it the value is the option's value or label.
match.title: Match

window.description: The window the step is done in: 0 the process's first, 1 the first one a step opened (a chooser, an approval), and so on.
window.title: Window

opens_window.description: The step opens a new window; the steps after it in the next window number are done there.
opens_window.title: Opens Window

closes_window.description: The step closes its window (a chooser, once something is chosen): its result shows in the window under it.
closes_window.title: Closes Window

dialogs.description: Dialogs of the browser itself the step brings up, in order, and how to answer them; one that was not recorded stops the run.
dialogs.title: Dialogs

when.description: Guard: skip the step if false.

otherwise.description: The other way the process goes: the step is done only when the step this names was not (forward the invoice, or hold it with a reason); its 'when' is checked after that.
otherwise.title: Otherwise

requires.description: What every recording showed before this step (the order's lines table still empty). When the screen shows otherwise, work left from before may be on it: the run stops before the step.

read_request.description: Owner-confirmed read-only POST during this step: exact path on the main application and literal form controls. Other requests remain guarded in a dry run.

per_line.description: Done once for each line of the record (an order's products): steps in a row marked so are one block, repeated line by line.
per_line.title: Per Line

calendar.description: For 'pick_date': how the calendar names days and months.

control.description: A check a person makes before confirming (four eyes: compares a request with its document, then approves it). Done by a person (executor 'human') unless the company lets the robot make it.
control.title: Control

clicks.description: For 'click': 2, a double click (a row of a list opens its record: WCR's requests to approve, Oracle Forms' lists).
clicks.title: Clicks

no_suggestion.description: For 'choose': when no suggestion contains the value, leave it typed and go on, as people did when the application had no such entry (the next step's result tells, e.g. a message that it was not found). Without it the run stops there.
no_suggestion.title: No Suggestion

repeat.description: For 'click': done again until something shows (a status that comes later).

find.description: For a step that saves and makes a document: the owner's way to find that document when the save's answer is lost (a read by the record's reference, and its row on a list). Without it a lost answer leaves the record to a person.

undo.description: For a step that saves and makes a document (a draft): the owner's rule for that document when the record cannot be finished in it (the application does not offer one of the record's values). Without it the document is left to a person.

Undo.description:
The owner's rule for the document a save made, when the record cannot be finished in it:
the robot removes it with ``target`` on the document's screen, only a document this record
made in this run and only while the independent read ``empty`` shows it there holding
nothing; the same read must then find it gone (benchmark week, p16: a draft request for an
index the ERP does not know). A dry run stops before the save that makes it anyway.

target.description: The control on the document's screen that removes it.
target.title: Target

empty.description: Reads the document: holds while it is there and holds nothing; a record not found (404) after the removal confirms it is gone.

Undo.title: Undo

ValueCheck.description:
A value of the record (or one read earlier on a screen) compared: a decision made from
the data, as people make it from their sheet ("Faktura zbiorcza: tak" ticks the box).

gt.description: The number it shows is greater.
gt.title: Gt

gte.description: The number it shows is at least this.
gte.title: Gte

lt.description: The number it shows is smaller.
lt.title: Lt

lte.description: The number it shows is at most this.
lte.title: Lte

ValueCheck.title: ValueCheck

WithinRow.description:
Restricts a step's target to one table row. 'only' refuses to guess between rows;
'newest' and 'oldest' take the row with the latest or earliest date in the column ``by``
(„the most recent pending order”); 'each' does the step in every row that fits, none being
fine (a box unticked in each row with an error).

by.description: For 'newest'/'oldest': the column whose dates order the rows.
by.title: By

where_not.description: Columns the row must not hold the value in (null: must not be empty: the rows with an error, benchmark M3).
where_not.title: Where Not

WithinRow.title: WithinRow

description: An executor-independent description of one business process.

card.description: What the process is for, as the people who do it say.

preconditions.description: What must hold before the process starts.
preconditions.title: Preconditions

records.description: The table people take the inputs from, row by row.

private.description: Screens show personal or confidential data: screenshots cover what is typed and what tables hold, and the model keeps no values from recordings.
private.title: Private

title: ProcessModel
